name: Guarded Thunderbrew Barrel
summary: In Kharanos, the Thunderbrew family’s ale waits under guard in the distillery cellar. Jarven watches over the stock.

sections.title: A Cellar Under Watch
sections.body: Jarven Thunderbrew keeps watch over the aging casks beneath the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos. Sentries stand beside the barrels, guarding the brew from tampering or theft.

sections.title: Family Pride and Rivalries
sections.body: The Thunderbrews keep their recipes close, especially the potent Thunder Ale. Dwarves give brewing the care they give smithing and mining. Troggs creep nearby, and brewing rivals compete across the Alliance. So Jarven watches until the family’s ale is ready to be tapped.

faq.q: Why can't I open this barrel?
aliases: why cant i touch the ale
faq.answer: Jarven Thunderbrew is keeping watch in the basement. While he guards the barrels, no one may disturb the Thunderbrew family’s stock.

Jarven Thunderbrew belongs to the Thunderbrew clan and is stationed in the Kharanos distillery cellar. He watches the family’s finest ales and keeps thieves and troublemakers from tampering with them.
The barrel rests in the cellar beneath the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos, Dun Morogh.

faq.q: Why do the Thunderbrews guard their ale so closely?
faq.answer: The Thunderbrews guard their ale because brewing is a revered craft and a family legacy to dwarves. Rival brewers, thieves, troggs, and leper gnomes threaten rare vintage barrels of Thunder Ale.

faq.q: Is this part of another quest?
faq.answer: Yes. You help Marleth Barleybrew with Bitter Rivals by slipping a barrel of Barleybrew Scalder among the Thunderbrews’ barrels of Thunder Ale.

faq.q: Can you distract or move Jarven?
faq.answer: Yes. Jarven has orders not to touch the stock, though he admits he would love a taste of Thunder Ale. Bring him one, and his attention turns from the barrels.

angles.text: As a dwarf, you know a family’s secret brew is worth defending with your life and limb. Jarven’s stubborn watch in the cellar comes naturally.
As a rogue, you know a quiet cellar heist grows harder with a vigilant dwarf watching the keg.
